subject: LexiconAI production: throughput/backpressure after model v1.3.0 release
messages:
From: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay.reddy@lexiconai.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: Maya Thompson <maya.thompson@lexiconai.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 22:10:00 +0000
Subject: Production throughput/backpressure after model v1.3.0 release

Hi Grace,

We're seeing a sharp regression in production since the 1.3.0 rollout that went live ~21:30 UTC. Symptoms: p99 generation latency ~2.1s -> ~5.0s, 500 errors up from 0.1% -> ~3.9%, and sustained throughput drop (~30% fewer tokens processed). This started immediately after the new quantization profile (q4_hybrid) was applied.

Attached: perf_dump_20270504.tar.gz and a short timeline screenshot.

Impact: user-facing timeouts for our autocomplete service, request rate limits we had to throttle on our side, and a spike in support tickets. We need:
- Immediate status and ETA for mitigation/rollback
- Whether you can route our traffic to the previous model variant while you investigate
- Any recommendations we can implement client-side to reduce errors in the short term

Please escalate internally — this is affecting our paid customers.

Thanks,
Sanjay Reddy
Head of Platform | LexiconAI
+1 415-555-0123

[attachment: perf_dump_20270504.tar.gz (perf logs)]

From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay.reddy@lexiconai.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 00:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production throughput/backpressure after model v1.3.0 release

Sanjay — thanks for the alert and the perf dump. We've pulled a brief timeline and started triage. Immediate notes:

- I have asked infra to open a hot rollback window to v1.2.9. That will require coordination but is our fastest path to restore baseline behavior.
- We're also testing a policy flip to route your traffic to a legacy quant profile (q4_legacy) while we root cause the kernel selection behavior.
- Can you confirm whether you applied any client-side changes at 21:30 UTC? Your timeline suggests the customer workload was unchanged on your end.

Next steps (I will own coordination):
1) Aditya and infra will validate rollback safety and estimate downtime window (~target 90m if safe).
2) We'll stage a canary flip for 10% of traffic immediately and monitor for errors.
3) If rollback is approved, we'll schedule it and share an exact ETA within 60 minutes.

Please confirm acceptance of a temporary failover to the older model variant and whether Lexicon is able to absorb a brief ~5–10 minute reconnection window during the rollback.

Grace O'Connor
Customer Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 01:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production throughput/backpressure after model v1.3.0 release

Grace / team — quick technical update from the runtime side after ingesting the perf dump:

Findings (short):
- Kernel selection latencies spike for sequence lengths > 512 when q4_hybrid is active; this correlates exactly with the customer p99 behavior.
- KV cache miss ratio increased; the new quant profile changed tensor layouts causing more cache evictions.
- Memory-backed batching fell into a suboptimal path that disables continuous batching for ~12% of requests.

Immediate mitigations I recommend:
1) Flip LexiconAI traffic to model v1.2.9 (current stable) — command we can run: sh /ops/routing/switch_model.sh --account lexiconai --from v1.3.0 --to v1.2.9 --window now
2) As a faster short-term knob, set the runtime flag --prefer-legacy-kernel for that traffic until we patch kernel selection (low risk).
3) Purge prefix caches for the customer to avoid stale KV behavior: redis-cli --scan --pattern "lexiconai:*" | xargs redis-cli del

I've attached perf_dump_20270504.tar.gz breakdown and timeline_screenshot.png showing the p99 delta. If Grace approves, infra can execute the routing flip; I estimate stabilization within 10–20 minutes post-flip.

Aditya Rao
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Team / Marissa — summarizing for execs and asking for quick sign-off on customer remediation:

Summary: LexiconAI (paid, multi-team customer) experienced a production throughput/latency regression immediately after our v1.3.0 release and quantization profile change. Customer-facing impact includes increased timeouts and ticket volume. Our runtime team (Aditya) recommends routing Lexicon traffic back to v1.2.9 immediately; Grace is coordinating.

Risks: potential churn and reputational impact. Lexicon asked for an ETA and indicated they may pause onboarding of a large enterprise client if not resolved within 24 hours.

Proposed exec actions (please approve):
- Pause the v1.3.0 progressive rollout until root cause is fixed (recommended).
- Offer Lexicon a one-time credit of $25,000 and a formal SLA exception letter.
- Priority bug fix: patch kernel selection path and release a small hotfix (target 72h).

Related items: HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/record/67890 (LexiconAI - account 67890). Internal ticket: INF-991.

If approved, I'll send the remediation note to Sanjay and coordinate the credit/process with finance and CS.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
